Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, hiring@zenith.ai
Date: 2026-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Zenith - ML coding screen: environment access + interviewer brief

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the quick replies and for confirming interest in the ML Engineer role at Zenith. We'd like to schedule a 60-minute technical screen focused on model debugging and a short coding exercise. Proposed slots below (PT):

- Thu, May 7 — 10:00–11:00
- Thu, May 7 — 14:00–15:00
- Fri, May 8 — 09:00–10:00

Please tell me which of these works for you and if you need a different timezone, happy to find another slot.

Logistics:
- Platform: CoderPad (we'll provide the session link once time is confirmed)
- Prep: No prior code to send; bring a laptop with Python 3.9.
- Attached: brief for the interviewers + your resume (for reference).

Interviewers (cc'd): Kimberly Park (senior ML), Ben Carter (infrastructure), Marcus Lin (hiring manager).

If the slot is confirmed, the internal team will follow up with a short interviewer run-of-show and rubric.

Best,
Grace

Kimberly / Ben / Marcus —

Alex confirmed the Thu, May 7 14:00 PT slot. Please find the run-of-show and interviewer brief attached. Key things to note:

- Goal: 60 minutes — 30–35 min coding/problem-solving (live CoderPad), 20–25 min model debugging/discussion, 5–10 min candidate questions and close.
- Candidate background: resume attached (see highlights page 2 — experience with NER pipelines and PyTorch optimizations).
- Scoring: use the attached rubric (we'll collect scores right after).
- Platform: CoderPad session (link below). Candidate may need an extra minute to pip-install; allow ~3–4 minutes at start.

CoderPad link (private): https://coderpad.io/session/5f3a9b
Drive brief: https://drive.google.com/zenith/brief-ml-screen

Attachments: zenith-coding-brief.pdf, interviewer-rubric.docx, candidate-resume-alex-ramos.pdf

Please reply with confirmations or last-minute constraints. If you can add one bullet about what you'll score for (e.g., correctness / system design tradeoffs / communication), I'll compile a single rubric summary to avoid duplication.

Thanks — Grace

Team —

Thanks for the quick debriefs. Quick notes from the interview and next steps:

- Candidate delivered a solid incremental solution in the coding prompt; correctness good, a few edge cases missing, handled in 28 minutes.
- Model debugging discussion was strong on failure modes and tradeoffs; Kimberly notes clear tradeoff articulation.
- Communication: calm and paced; matched interview length.
- Action items: please fill the shared scoring sheet (Drive link in the brief) by end of day tomorrow. Recommend: hold for on-site decision until we get Marcus' final score; Marcus to post hire/no-hire recommendation.

Alex is interested in moving forward; Grace will coordinate recruiter touchpoint about potential on-site timing and comp band.

Thanks all — Grace
